Rishi Patel: Heads-up — GCP sent a pricing bulletin: effective immediately, nvidia-a100 GPU hourly unit cost in eu-west1 increased ~18%. I can see it reconciled on this morning's invoice snapshot.
Maya Chen: ugh. I just ran the unit-econ scripts, rough first pass shows ~+12% per-token compute cost for our EU-hosted requests if we keep current batching/kv cache.
Alex Gomez: are we seeing any capacity constraints or just price changes?
Rishi Patel: primarily price. No immediate quota changes in the console. A couple of preemptible pools spiked in spot price but reserved pools unchanged.
ops-bot: [Alert] billing/price-change/eu-west1 — provider update received at 2026-03-18T08:12Z.
Luis Ortega: can we route more non-latency-sensitive workload to us-central1 where list prices stable? What’s the routing delta?
Maya Chen: routing helps but adds egress and multi-region tail latency. Quick calc: moving 30% of EU inference to US adds ~2.5ms median and ~$0.005/token in egress for certain customers. Net savings narrow.
Caroline: finance-team — @finance-bot, can you post the delta impact on committed-reserve margins if we keep current pricing vs pass-through?
finance-bot: Quick numbers from invoice: baseline EU GPU op cost 1.00 -> new 1.18. If we absorb increase across hosted API, gross margin hit ~3.4 percentage points on current ARR mix. If we pass-through to premium EU customers only, hit on self-serve ARR ~1.8pp. Estimates rough.
Alex Gomez: ok. Ops-side mitigations: 1) shift lower-SLO traffic to quantized model variants (2) increase batching window slightly for EU pools (3) opportunistic re-routing to cheaper regions for background jobs. Any estimate for batching gains?
Maya Chen: increasing batching TTL from 8ms -> 15ms predicted ~6-8% drop in tokens/sec cost on EU pools but adds tail-p99 latency ~12-18ms for some customers. Need to run eval on latency-sensitive routes.
Rishi Patel: also we can adjust Dedicated autoscaler to prefer pre-booked capacity (reserved nodes) for steady loads and avoid on-demand bursts that are most affected. That requires updating rollout policy for a subset of customers.
Luis Ortega: for Reserved capacity planning: do we recommend expanding EU reservations to lock price? Current commit term modeling shows buying +10% reserved capacity at current commit price reduces exposure but increases carrying cost if demand softens.
Caroline: finance prefers a hybrid: lock for baseline steady load (75th percentile) and leave buffer for burst on ondemand. We need specific commit sizing from infra.
Maya Chen: I'll run per-route steady-state percentile and return a recommended reservation size with sensitivity to +/-20% demand.
Rishi Patel: also flagging cluster health: eu-west1 PG2 racks showing slightly higher GPU ECC counts last 48h, engineering investigating — if hardware replacement ramps up, replacement capacity might push use to on-demand where price spike hurts more.
Alex Gomez: good point. If hardware churn continues, reserved strategy could be less effective. We should factor replacement churn into the commit sizing model.
Caroline: next steps: Maya to produce reservation sizing + latency impact for batching changes by EOD; Rishi to post hardware-churn risk and expected timing; Finance to provide pricing pass-through templates and impact on packaging (tier thresholds) within 24h.
Rishi Patel: noted. Also will create a quick internal note for sales/CS about potential billing/pricing messaging: quick bullet points for customers on EU price volatility and options (reserved, regional routing, model quantization). :memo:
Luis Ortega: also recommending we run a short A/B in EU: 10% traffic apply batching+quantized variant, measure P50/P95 and unit-econ over 6 hours. If uplift in margin without unacceptable latency, roll to 50%.
Maya Chen: scheduled A/B and will post results in #eng-infra thread when ready.
Caroline: thanks all. @ops-bot drop a reminder in 24h for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
